composition.title: Memory allocation
composition.note: Blocks are what the scheduler books: a dGPU slice books its limit plus the runtime overhead held outside it. The black line is what the card has in use now.

tooltip.actualVRAM: Memory the HAMi interception counts for the slice; nvidia-smi shows about 0.4 GiB more per process (its CUDA context)
tooltip.smReference: A sampled reference: slices time-sharing the SMs jump between 0 and 100 per sample; the details chart shows a 1-minute average

quota.title: Change dGPU quota
quota.help: The memory limit of each replica on each card; it takes effect when saved.
quota.note: The new limit applies to running instances at once (the scheduler's books and the HAMi memory limit move together). Engines that size their KV cache at start, such as vLLM and SGLang, use it only after their instances are restarted from the deployment page; engines that allocate as they go use it right away. When lowering, an instance already holding more than the new limit keeps its limit until it restarts.
quota.applied_one: The memory limit is now {{limit}}; {{count}} running instance took it at once.
quota.applied_other: The memory limit is now {{limit}}; {{count}} running instances took it at once.
quota.appliedDeployment: The deployment's memory limit is now {{limit}}; the instances it starts from now on run under it.
quota.pendingTitle_one: {{count}} instance keeps its limit until it restarts:
quota.pendingTitle_other: {{count}} instances keep their limit until they restart:

pending.backend: its partition backend reads the limit only at start
pending.asleep: it is asleep; a lower limit could fail its wake
pending.starting: it is starting; a lower limit could fail its start
pending.in_use: it holds {{used}}, more than the new {{limit}}
pending.no_usage: it reports no memory use, so a lower limit is not risked
